claim: The IEA base case is bracketed by alternative cases (Lift-Off, High Efficiency, Headwinds). Efficiency gains in AI hardware and software could materially lower the 2030 figure; the report itself flags this uncertainty.

source.name: IEA, Energy and AI (full report PDF)

claim: Fingrid's own study shows the Finnish constraint is grid connectability, not price: 70% of generation sits in the west and north, over 50% of consumption in the south. Cheap power that cannot be connected does not attract load.

source.name: Fingrid news: locating industrial facilities close to generation increases connectability

claim: [DEMODATA, world situation 2] The guidance cut is concentrated in non-AI cloud capacity at two companies; AI-specific capex guidance was reaffirmed. Demand for AI data centres may continue even as the total falls.
[DEMODATA, world situation 2] The DRAM price fall is led by PC and mobile grades; server DRAM allocation to AI customers is unchanged, so industrial buyers may not see relief.
[DEMODATA, world situation 2] The two withdrawn agreements were speculative filings; the remaining 3 GW continue toward energisation on the published timetable.
[DEMODATA, world situation 2] The copper decline reflects an unwind of speculative positions; physical premiums and grid-related orders remain firm.
[DEMODATA, world situation 2] The postponement concerns two of four sites; the Hamina expansion and the Loviisa power agreement continue unchanged.
[DEMODATA, world situation 2] Most cancellations are of announcements that never entered construction; capacity under construction is unchanged.

Jonathan Koomey and co-authors find that data-centre electricity forecasts are biased toward overestimation: duplicate and speculative interconnection requests inflate expected load, service-demand growth and efficiency gains are both uncertain, and historical utility forecasts have consistently overshot. Projections of explosive growth should be discounted, not taken at face value.

source.name: Koomey Analytics and GridLab, Separating fact from fiction in data center electricity forecasts: a guide for regulators (Koomey, Schmidt, Sreedharan, Kumar, McNair, 2026)

LUT University (May 2026) finds continuous data-centre supply from new renewables technically and economically feasible in Finland at about EUR 103–121/MWh, and more than 7.2 GW of permitted wind and solar is ready to build; the price impact of new load can be mitigated if data centres bring their own generation.

source.name: LUT University, Researchers find answer to data centres' massive electricity demand (May 2026)
